_readme: Single source of truth for the homepage bench table, tested picks, 'on our radar' list, ticker and cost calculator. To publish a new hands-on review: add an entry to 'tested' (newest first), put a 480x640 card image at images/card_<slug>.webp, and run node build.js. ptt = measured PTT delay text, or null if not timed. cost = {hw: per-radio USD, renew: per-radio per-year USD after year 1, src: where the fee came from} or null if not confirmed.

tested.name: Radtel P8
tested.bestAt: Clear, loud audio and a solid zinc-alloy body
tested.watchOut: 1–2 s PTT delay; no published IP rating
tested.desc: Clear, loud audio and a body that feels premium for the price, with SIMs included for the first year (about $10 per card per year after, per Radtel). Expect a 1 to 2 second pause after you press PTT.

cost.src: Radtel: 2-pack from ~$99; about $10 per SIM per year after year 1

tested.name: ChoYong WT2
tested.cat: Handheld · PoC + UHF + SW/AM/FM + internet radio
tested.bestAt: PoC, analog UHF, shortwave and internet radio in one
tested.watchOut: Use 2.4 GHz WiFi for PoC; compact for big hands
tested.desc: A PoC radio, a 2W analog UHF walkie-talkie and a TEF6686 shortwave/AM/FM receiver with internet radio, all in one handheld. PTT was excellent on 2.4 GHz WiFi; the analog UHF side is weak, as expected at 2W.

tested.name: OMIZN M9
tested.bestAt: Rugged aluminum body, great sound, readable screen
tested.watchOut: Heavy at 300 g; no public group directory
tested.desc: An aluminum alloy body and dust-proof, noise-reducing speaker that earn the outdoor pitch, with great sound and an easy-to-read screen. It is heavier than most, and there is no public directory for finding other users.

tested.name: TIDRADIO TD-M2 Pro
tested.bestAt: Two PTT buttons: nationwide PoC plus local FRS
tested.watchOut: Odmaster app is buggy; groups are hard to find
tested.desc: The cheapest way into dual-mode: PTT1 talks over LTE nationwide, PTT2 drops to license-free FRS when there is no signal. Solid in hand with clear audio. The Odmaster app is the weak spot.

cost.src: TIDRADIO: first year free, published $9.99 per year after

tested.name: Wouxun KG-WV9
tested.bestAt: Group and member calling built into the radio menu
tested.watchOut: Not sold through US retail; quote-only
tested.desc: Group and member calling run from the radio's own menu, with no app needed mid-call, backed by Wouxun's long two-way radio track record. Ordered direct from Wouxun or a distributor.

tested.name: CARRBORG X13
tested.bestAt: Bright screen, clear audio, no data subscription
tested.watchOut: More PTT lag than faster rivals; large body
tested.desc: A genuinely bright, easy-to-read screen and clear voice audio, with lifetime free data that undercuts most rivals on long-term cost. A touch more PTT lag than faster radios, and a big body for small hands.

cost.src: Seller listing: lifetime free data included

radar.name: Inrico T320
radar.note: Android PoC radio that runs Zello; popular with preppers. Spec-based overview.

radar.name: GLOBAL-PTT 5288 Plus
radar.note: PoC plus an 8W analog VHF/UHF fallback. Spec-based overview.

radar.name: Hytera PNC360S
radar.note: Built around Hytera's Horizon web dispatch and GPS fleet map. Spec-based overview.

radar.name: Motorola WAVE PTX
radar.note: Enterprise PTT platform that can bridge into land-mobile radio. Spec-based overview.
